plainTitle: City Council refused a 7-storey building at 922 Millwood Road

sources.label: Revised staff report from the Director, Community Planning, North York District

whatIsProposed.text: The owner asked to change the Official Plan and the zoning rules for 922 Millwood Road to build a 7-storey building. It would have homes above and a small shop on the ground floor. City Council said no.

citations.quote: The application proposes a 7-storey (21 metres plus 4 metre mechanical penthouse and rooftop amenity space) mixed-use building at 922 Millwood Road.
City Council refuse the application to amend the Official Plan for the lands municipally known as 922 Millwood Road.

whatIsProposed.text: The building would have 44 homes, 29 car parking spaces underground and 52 bicycle parking spaces. Most homes would have one bedroom.

citations.quote: The proposal includes 44 dwelling units, 33 one-bedroom (75%), 6 two-bedroom (13.6%), and 5 three-bedroom units (11.4%).
The proposal includes a total of 29 vehicular parking spaces (25 resident and 4 visitor)
A total of 52 bicycle parking spaces

whatIsProposed.text: The top floor would hold only shared amenity space and equipment, with no homes. It would cover about half the roof.

citations.quote: The seventh storey is a partial storey and consists solely of amenity space and mechanical penthouse and is limited to approximately 50 percent of the roof area.

whatIsProposed.text: The plan is smaller than first proposed. The original application asked for 8 storeys and 60 homes.

citations.quote: The original application was for an 8 storey (26.3 metres plus a 4 metre mechanical penthouse) residential building
60 residential dwelling units and 29 vehicular parking spaces

whatIsProposed.text: The site is empty now. It used to hold a one-storey dry cleaner.

citations.quote: The site is generally flat and is currently vacant.
The subject site was previously occupied by a single storey dry-cleaning establishment

why.text: The site is in an area planned for low-rise homes, where buildings can be up to four storeys. A 7-storey building needed a change to the Official Plan.

citations.quote: While the Neighbourhoods designation only permits buildings up to four storeys in height
An Official Plan Amendment application is required to permit a 7-storey mixed-use building in a Neighbourhoods designation.

why.text: City staff supported the building. They said Millwood Road already has a mix of building types, and that nearby apartment buildings range from three to seven storeys.
why.caveat: This is the opinion of City staff. City Council did not follow it.

citations.quote: Staff are of the opinion that the proposed 7-storey residential apartment building is an acceptable form of modest intensification
a number of existing apartment buildings with heights ranging from three to seven storeys

why.text: City Council voted 12 to 11 to refuse the application.
why.caveat: The City's item page does not state Council's reasons for refusing.

citations.quote: City Council refuse the application to amend City of Toronto Zoning By-law 569-2013
Yes: 12
No: 11

whoIsAffected.text: The site is at the northeast corner of Millwood Road and Randolph Road, in Ward 15 (Don Valley West).

citations.quote: The site is located at the north east corner of Millwood Road and Randolph Road.

whoIsAffected.text: People in the two-storey houses across Krawchuk Lane to the north: cars and delivery trucks would use a driveway off the lane.

citations.quote: Krawchuk Lane and two-storey single detached homes to the north.
Parking and loading are proposed to be accessed via a private driveway from Krawchuk Lane.

whoIsAffected.text: At a public meeting run by staff, about 98 people attended. Concerns included height, traffic, parking, shadows and privacy. Some people supported more housing.

citations.quote: attended by approximately 98 members of the public
Concerns regarding shadowing, privacy, overlook, setbacks, and impacts on adjacent residential properties
Support for additional housing, mixed-use development, walkability, and senior housing options.

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: The owner may appeal the refusal to the Ontario Land Tribunal. Council allowed the City's lawyer to defend the decision there if that happens.
conditionsAndUnknowns.caveat: This page has not checked whether an appeal was filed.

citations.quote: City Council authorize the City Solicitor to attend at the Ontario Land Tribunal if the matter is appealed and to retain outside consultants as necessary.

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: Before its vote on the item, the community council voted to add requests for privacy screening on the rooftop and a less blank side wall.

citations.quote: appropriate buffer / screening is provided between the rooftop amenity area and the residential neighbourhood across Krawchuk Lane
Forwarded this item to City Council without recomendation.

conditionsAndUnknowns.caveat: City Council refused the application, so the record does not show these requests as part of any approval.

citations.quote: This report reviews and recommends approval of the application

committee.text: The community council held the public meeting. A motion to approve the item lost, 2 to 3, so it went to City Council with no recommendation either way.

citations.quote: Forwarded this item to City Council without recomendation.
Result: Lost Majority Required Total members that voted Yes: 2

council.text: City Council refused the Official Plan and zoning changes, against staff's advice.

citations.quote: City Council adopted this item on July 29 and 30, 2026 with amendments.
City Council refuse the application to amend the Official Plan for the lands municipally known as 922 Millwood Road.

whatHappensNext.text: The building cannot go ahead under this decision. If the owner appeals, the Ontario Land Tribunal would decide the matter.
whatHappensNext.caveat: The record does not say whether an appeal has been made.

citations.quote: if the matter is appealed
